comm-update-git-branch.SKILL.md:
---
name: comm-update-git-branch
description: Use when resuming deferred branch work, synchronizing with integration, or preserving unfinished changes on a fresh base.
---

# Update a working branch

Inputs: task, repository/branch, agreed dependencies and authorized update.

1. Read harness/common/skills/comm-commit-task-stages/references/work-safety.md
   before mutation and
   harness/common/skills/comm-verify-project-facts/references/git-base-state.md
   for identity, fresh target and recorded SHAs. Inspect divergence and both changesets.
2. Before choosing preservation read [methods](references/methods.md).
   Agree unresolved choices; a necessary feature dependency never excuses stale
   integration. Incorporate missing target changes before resumed implementation.
3. For explicit conflicts or relevant semantic overlap read
   [conflicts](references/conflicts.md). Unknown intent/authority blocks dependent edits.
4. Verify saved behavior with the combined affected contracts on the resulting
   stable revision. Use comm-test-project-behavior, comm-assess-project-tests and
   comm-run-project-checks for application changes; harness checks use comm-validate-harness-instructions separately.
   Old green results do not verify the new version.
5. Recheck the target before final checks/integration under the base-state owner.
   Finish with labeled fields `old=<full SHA or unknown>`,
   `target=<full SHA or unknown>`, `result=<full SHA or not created>`,
   preservation, executed checks and gaps.

Done: work is compatible with the checked integration version, or a precise stop.
No push/PR/merge/deletion or local mutation within PR operations is granted.
Protected-harness changes retain inbox gates.
comm-update-git-branch.references/methods.md:
# Preserve unfinished work

A: new branch from fresh integration plus controlled transfer of necessary work.
Useful for partial/mixed old work; inspect dependencies, already integrated
changes and omissions. Use comm-create-git-branch; preserve the source.
B: update the existing task branch by the project's authorized method.
Useful for cohesive continuing work/PR identity; assess conflicts and collaborators.
Never prescribe merge, rebase or cherry-pick universally. Published-history
restrictions remain; do not rewrite others' base or force-publish automatically.
Keep deliberate feature dependencies distinct from stale ancestry.

Do not stash/commit foreign work to clean the tree. Local commits use
comm-commit-task-stages and ce-commit, including commits produced by integration;
choose an operation mode that preserves this gate or stop. During PR operations
the local branch stays read only; necessary preparation requires an agreed
separate scope, never an automatic context switch.
comm-update-git-branch.references/conflicts.md:
# Resolve intended behavior

Inspect the common base and both changesets; preserve current approved contracts,
not obsolete code deliberately superseded. Never blanket-select ours/theirs.
Unclear or incompatible intent: show the conflict, propose a resolution and wait.
Database and other protected-domain approvals remain mandatory.

Follow renamed destinations, update affected callers for interface changes, and
regenerate generated/lock files from reconciled inputs using project tools.
Do not assume one side's generated output is the combined result.
Inspect silent conflicts: versions/formats, cache/build IDs and old API callers.
Review actual resolved changes before staging; check unresolved markers and
agreed decisions. Symbols, clean status and no markers alone prove no behavior.
Select checks for both sides' affected contracts, overlaps and dependencies
through existing test owners, not only the old task diff.
